verdictRationale: The spec is much stronger than the rough idea, but it still leaves several enforceability gaps that would let implementation invent critical behavior around approval integrity, model access, and install/update semantics. These are fixable in the spec before build starts, so this should continue rather than rescope.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A mocked apply or promote run can write or update an artifact after approval using a stale proposal/config state that no longer satisfies the current control-plane policy.
falsifiability.observableSignal: The promoted draft or updated proposal exists on disk even though the proposal was modified after approval, the output path was removed from the allowlist, or required validation failed.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Create a temp installed root, approve a valid proposal, then mutate its content or control-plane output_paths before invoking promote; assert the command re-loads current proposal/config, detects approval invalidation, and exits nonzero without creating or modifying draft artifacts.
falsifiability.threshold: zero unauthorized writes across apply, approve, reject, and promote commands

newIssueList.title: Approval integrity is underspecified
newIssueList.description: The spec says promotion requires an approved proposal, but it does not define whether approval is bound to the exact proposal content that was reviewed. A proposal could be approved, later appended with new evidence or modified by dedupe, and then promoted under an old approval. That breaks the safety claim that operator approval gates the actual artifact being promoted.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add an approval record with proposal content hash, approver identity or local operator marker, approved_at, approved_target, and validation hash. Any proposal mutation after approval must reset promotion_status to proposed or require re-approval.
newIssueList.lineRef: CLI / Dedupe And Cooldown / Proposal Schema

newIssueList.title: Model reviewer access is not constrained enough
newIssueList.description: The spec says the model reviewer is optional and receives redacted bundles, but it does not define a strict tool sandbox or execution boundary. Under adversarial logs, a model reviewer could be implemented in a normal agent context with filesystem, shell, Notion, Slack, or memory write access. The design stance explicitly wanted scoped reviewer access, but the current spec only constrains prompts and output paths, not available tools.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Specify that model review runs in a no-tool or read-only sandbox with no shell, no Notion/Jira/Slack/Gmail writes, no memory_write, and no filesystem writes. Treat model output as data that only the deterministic orchestrator may validate and persist.
newIssueList.lineRef: Review Pipeline / Redaction And Safety / Hermes-Agent Inspiration

newIssueList.title: Install and update behavior lacks conflict semantics
newIssueList.description: The spec requires fresh installs and additive updates, but it does not say how managed files are identified, versioned, or merged when an existing installed root has local edits to the same workflow, command, skill, or config path. Without a managed-file manifest or conflict policy, implementation could overwrite operator configuration while still claiming to be additive. This is especially risky because the feature is explicitly default-installed.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define a managed template manifest with source version, checksum, destination, and merge policy. Updates may write missing files, create .new or migration-plan entries on checksum mismatch, and must not overwrite locally modified control-plane config or proposals.
newIssueList.lineRef: Runtime Surfaces / Phases P2 / Rollout-related acceptance criteria

newIssueList.title: Score dimensions are named but not operationalized
newIssueList.description: Scoring is described as deterministic, but dimensions such as severity, reuse, confidence, blast radius, and staleness still lack concrete mappings from evidence to 0-5 values. Different implementers could produce incompatible scores and churn behavior while satisfying the prose. This weakens the threshold guarantee because total >= 18 is only meaningful if the score rubric is stable.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add a compact scoring rubric table for each dimension with 0, 1-2, 3-4, and 5 bands tied to observable evidence counts, age windows, project counts, failure categories, and risk classes.

newIssueList.title: Path allowlist needs symlink and traversal rules
newIssueList.description: The spec says every write checks target paths against output_paths, but it does not define canonicalization, symlink handling, or ancestor directory creation rules. A malicious or corrupted installed root could place symlinks under the allowed self-improvement directories that redirect writes into live shared surfaces or source files. A string-prefix allowlist would pass while violating the no-live-mutation invariant.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Require realpath canonicalization after parent creation, reject symlinked output directories and path traversal, and test that allowed relative paths cannot escape the installed root or drafts/proposals directories.
newIssueList.lineRef: Control Plane / Redaction And Safety / Validations

newIssueList.title: Proposal mutation rules are incomplete
newIssueList.description: Dedupe can append evidence to an active proposal, approve/reject can update status, and promotion can update state, but the spec does not define atomic writes, file locking, or concurrent scheduled/manual runs. A scheduled apply and manual approval could race, producing partial YAML, lost evidence, or approvals against mid-write content. This matters because the feature explicitly supports both scheduled and on-demand execution.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Specify atomic write via temp file plus rename, per-proposal locking, and command behavior when a proposal is locked. Add a concurrency test with overlapping apply and approve/promote operations.
newIssueList.lineRef: Dedupe And Cooldown / CLI / Scheduler acceptance criteria

newIssueList.title: External source authorization is vague
newIssueList.description: External evidence is disabled by default, but the spec does not define what proves a source is explicitly configured and authorized or how credentials are kept out of evidence bundles. A future implementation could treat any locally available connector or environment token as authorization. That would conflict with the stated privacy and Notion workspace constraints.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add an external_sources schema with source id, enabled flag, allowed scopes, local cache path, credential reference by name only, and a requirement that raw connector credentials never enter evidence manifests, model prompts, reports, or proposals.
newIssueList.lineRef: Control Plane / Evidence Model / What's NOT in v0

newIssueList.title: Root path examples conflict with canonical paths
newIssueList.description: The spec says source templates install under harness/shared_factory, while some evidence examples still refer to shared_factory/06-runs-and-logs without the harness prefix. It also says older top-level shared_factory roots are legacy input roots only. The mixed wording could cause tests or docs to accidentally read or write the wrong tree.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Normalize every runtime path example to harness/shared_factory unless explicitly labeled legacy read-only input. Add one acceptance check that top-level shared_factory is never written.
newIssueList.lineRef: Evidence Model / Review Pipeline / Acceptance Criteria

preserveList.summary: The spec correctly preserves the central safety boundary: v0 may write proposals, reports, and drafts, but must not mutate live shared skills, commands, workflows, automations, Notion, shell configuration, or harness globals.
The runtime surface list is concrete enough to guide implementation around canonical installed paths and separates runs, proposals, and drafts.
The dry-run versus apply distinction is strong: dry-run writes nothing, while apply writes only run records and proposal files under the self-improvement log tree.

The proposal schema includes the right core contract fields: evidence, deterministic findings, optional model recommendation, score, approval requirement, validation plan, redaction status, and promotion status.

The validation plan targets the most important risk areas, including redaction, path allowlists, invalid sidecars, scheduler resilience, and holdout fixtures with prompt-injection and secret-shaped strings.
